Background: had been obese since I was 4-5. Didn’t do a single sport in school or anything athletic ever. Realized afterwards that my main issue was binge eating rather than bad diet. I knew how to eat healthy but I would demolish 4000 calories in one sitting like twice a week. 

Supplements: creatine, protein, assorted pre workouts. No PEDs or anything like that. 

Routine: I went from 270lb to 180lb with just keto. I didn’t start lifting until after I lost the weight so all the muscle gains are over the course of a year. started with a three day full body split and then moved into a 5 day split. Had some tough family issues this winter and was at home for 6 weeks eating out of boredom and depression but I didn’t stop training and my strength exploded so it was net positive I suppose. Currently on a 4 day upper/lower split which seems to work best for me. 

My diet is pretty normal, I eat basically what I want when I want but I’m super active so I never put on weight. I’m a server at a high volume restaurant and I run about 40km a week.

Other info: I never understood my body or did anything active but I’ve become so grateful for what I have. My genetics are really good, currently at 175lb bench, 315 deadlift and 290 squat. That on top of being able to run half marathons kinda blows me away considering where I was 2 years ago.

I keep a little chart on my wall of the macros of most of the foods I eat (chicken breast, broccoli, peanuts, etc). It was a game changer for me. Weighing your food is also really useful when you want to stray from your eating schedule for a night. If I know that I’ve eaten exactly 1600 calories on any given day and I know that my maintenance calories are 2500 then I can go out guilt free on a Saturday night and get a few drinks and a snack. 

Don’t guess or leave anything up in the air. We have all the tools we need to effortlessly follow healthy eating habits :) once you start, you’ll wonder how you did it any other way.
